items.title: Home Assistant MCP Server
items.text:
The Home Assistant MCP server is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for controlling and monitoring Home Assistant from MCP clients like Claude Desktop.

Use this documentation to:

  • Understand the capabilities of the server
  • Set up Docker-based or local development environments
  • Configure environment variables and the optional PostgreSQL cache
  • Discover available MCP tools for device control and monitoring

If you are integrating this server with Claude Desktop, see the getting started guide for example configuration.

items.title: cache
items.text:
Cache layer for Home Assistant MCP services.

Cache is the facade the app uses. It serializes values as JSON, keeps hit/miss statistics, and never raises into the request path: backend errors are logged (rate limited), counted in CacheStats.errors, and turned into misses.

Backends: - PostgresBackend: a table in the service's own PostgreSQL database (DATABASE_URL). Connects lazily, backs off for 30 s after any database error, and creates its table on first use. - MemoryBackend: a process-local dict for local development and tests (CACHE_BACKEND=memory).

items.title: PostgresBackend
items.text:
PostgresBackend(conninfo: str, clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic)

Cache table in PostgreSQL via a small sync connection pool.

Constructing it does no I/O. The pool opens on the first operation, the table is created once per process after the first successful connect, and any database error starts a 30 s backoff during which every operation is a miss and is_connected() is False (it never does I/O itself).

items.title: CacheTTL
items.text:
Standard TTL values for Home Assistant data types.

All values can be overridden via environment variables by prefixing with CACHE_TTL_ For example: CACHE_TTL_HA_STATES=5 will set HA_STATES to 5 seconds

Environment Variables

CACHE_TTL_HA_STATES: Entity states cache (default: 3 seconds) CACHE_TTL_HA_DEVICE_LIST: Device metadata cache (default: 1800 seconds) CACHE_TTL_HA_ENTITY_LIST: Entity metadata cache (default: 1800 seconds) CACHE_TTL_HA_AREAS: Area list cache (default: 3600 seconds) CACHE_TTL_HA_SERVICES: Service list cache (default: 3600 seconds)

items.title: glob_to_like
items.text:
glob_to_like(glob: str) -> str

Translate a cache-key glob into a SQL LIKE pattern (used with ESCAPE '\').

* matches any run of characters and ? any single character; every other character is literal, so %, _ and \ in the glob are escaped. Character classes ([abc]) are not supported and match literally.

items.title: Configuration
items.text: The Home Assistant MCP server is configured through environment variables, typically via .env.local when running with Docker Compose.

items.title: Core Environment Variables
items.text: Variable Required Default Description HA_URL Yes - Home Assistant URL (e.g. http://homeassistant.local) HA_TOKEN Yes - Long-lived access token HA_VERIFY_SSL No true Verify SSL certificates DEBUG No false Enable debug logging DATABASE_URL No - PostgreSQL URL for the response cache CACHE_BACKEND No - memory for a process-local cache (local development)

items.title: Cache
items.text:
The cache is optional. CACHE_BACKEND=memory selects a process-local cache; otherwise a set DATABASE_URL selects PostgreSQL; with neither, every request goes to Home Assistant.

DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@host:5432/homeassistant_mcp?sslmode=require&application_name=homeassistant-mcp

The PostgreSQL backend:

  • connects lazily on first use (startup never waits for the database);
  • creates its table, cache_entries (an UNLOGGED table: a database crash may empty it), on first connect. The database user needs CREATE on schema public; if it lacks it, the server logs a warning naming the fix (GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA public TO <user>, run as postgres);
  • never fails a request: after any database error it logs (at most once a minute per operation), serves misses and calls Home Assistant directly for 30 seconds, then retries.

clear_cache takes a glob: * matches any run of characters and ? one character; character classes ([abc]) are not supported. get_cache_info reports the database host and name, never credentials.

items.title: Cache TTLs
items.text:
Override with CACHE_TTL_<NAME> (seconds):

Name Default Data HA_STATES 3 Entity states HA_DEVICE_LIST 1800 Device metadata HA_ENTITY_LIST 1800 Entity metadata HA_AREAS 3600 Area list HA_SERVICES 3600 Service list

items.title: Deployment Notes
items.text:
• For Docker Compose, edits to .env.local are picked up on restart.
  • For direct execution (without Docker), you can export variables in your shell before running server.py or server_remote.py.

items.title: Getting Started
items.text: This guide walks through setting up the Home Assistant MCP server and connecting it to your Home Assistant instance.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• Docker and Docker Compose (for containerized deployment)
  • A running Home Assistant instance (local or remote)
  • A long-lived access token from your Home Assistant profile
  • Network access from the server to Home Assistant

items.title: Clone and Configure
items.text:
cd homeassistant-mcp
cp .env.example .env.local

Edit .env.local and set at least:

HA_URL=http://homeassistant.local:8123
HA_TOKEN=your-long-lived-access-token-here
HA_VERIFY_SSL=true
DEBUG=false

You can also enable the optional cache here: CACHE_BACKEND=memory for local development, or DATABASE_URL for a PostgreSQL database (see Configuration).

items.title: Run with Docker Compose
items.text:
docker-compose up --build

The server will start in stdio mode inside the container, ready to accept MCP connections.

items.title: Connect to Claude Desktop
items.text:
Update your Claude Desktop configuration file:

  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json
  • Windows: %APPDATA%\\Claude\\claude_desktop_config.json

Example configuration:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "homeassistant": {
      "command": "docker",
      "args": ["compose", "-f", "/path/to/homeassistant-mcp/docker-compose.yml", "run", "--rm", "homeassistant-mcp"]
    }
  }
}

Restart Claude Desktop to activate the server.

items.title: MCP Tools
items.text:
The Home Assistant MCP server exposes tools for device control, automation, and monitoring via the Home Assistant API.

Major categories include:

  • Lights: turn_on_light, turn_off_light, toggle_light, set_light_brightness
